# Agent environments

## What an environment is
State, observations, actions, dynamics. The reward is a separate claim about what matters.

## Partial observability (POMDP)
When the agent cannot see the full state it must maintain a belief and sometimes act to gather information. Measurement can be an action with a cost.

## Attention as a hidden variable
Learners do not read everything shown to them. Attention gates learning and drains with fatigue.

# Evaluating agents

## pass@k vs pass^k
pass@k: any of k runs succeeds. pass^k: all k succeed. Reliability is what deployment needs.

## Proxy vs direct measures
A quiz score is a proxy. Retention a week later is closer to the thing itself.

args.text:
Yes — POMDP stands for *Partially Observable Markov Decision Process*.

In this class context, it means the agent does not get to see the full true state of the environment directly. Instead, it sees observations that only reveal part of the state, so it has to keep track of beliefs / hidden state and sometimes take actions to gather information.

A simple writeup sentence you can use:
‘Because the agent cannot directly observe the full state, this environment is partially observable (a POMDP); it must infer hidden variables from observations and may need to take information-gathering actions.’
